Strings, sequences and regular expressions

Source: vignettes/strings-regex.Rmd
strings-regex.Rmd
library(z3r)
ctx <- z3_context()

Z3 strings are Unicode sequences. R character values convert to them exactly, escapes and all, and results come back as UTF-8.

String constraints 

s <- z3_string(ctx, "s")
t <- z3_string(ctx, "t")
sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol,
  z3_concat(s, "-", t) == "alpha-beta",
  z3_length(s) > z3_length(t) - 2,
  z3_prefixof("al", s))
z3_check(sol)
#> [1] "sat"
m <- z3_model(sol)
c(s = z3_value(z3_eval(m, s)), t = z3_value(z3_eval(m, t)))
#>       s       t 
#> "alpha"  "beta"

Positions are 0-based, as in SMT-LIB:

hello <- z3_string_val(ctx, "hello")
val <- function(e) z3_value(z3_simplify(e))
c(substr = val(z3_substr(hello, 1, 3)), at = val(z3_str_at(hello, 4)),
  index = val(z3_indexof(hello, "l")), last = val(z3_last_indexof(hello, "l")),
  replace = val(z3_replace(hello, "l", "L")))
#>  substr      at   index    last replace 
#>   "ell"     "o"     "2"     "3" "heLlo"
val(z3_str_to_int(z3_string_val(ctx, "1234")))
#> [1] 1234
val(z3_int_to_str(z3_int_val(ctx, 99)))
#> [1] "99"

escaped = TRUE reads SMT-LIB escapes such as \u{e9}, and z3_string_escaped() writes them back. Raw vectors convert both ways for strings whose characters are all below U+0100:

cafe <- z3_string_val(ctx, "caf\\u{e9}", escaped = TRUE)
z3_value(cafe) == "caf\u00e9"
#> [1] TRUE
z3_string_escaped(cafe)
#> [1] "caf\\u{e9}"
z3_string_bytes(z3_string_val(ctx, "Z3"))
#> [1] 5a 33

Regular expressions

Regular expressions are built from strings and combinators; a plain string is accepted wherever a regular expression is expected:

digit <- z3_re_range("0", "9", ctx)
lower <- z3_re_range("a", "z", ctx)
id <- z3_re_concat(z3_re_plus(lower), "_", z3_re_loop(digit, 2, 4))
sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol, z3_in_re(s, id), z3_length(s) == 8, z3_contains(s, "zz"))
z3_check(sol)
#> [1] "sat"
z3_value(z3_eval(z3_model(sol), s))
#> [1] "mpzzk_24"

Regular expressions also prove properties. A character that is not a digit is “any character” intersected with the complement of the digits; no non-empty number is made only of such characters:

any_char <- z3_re_allchar(z3_re_sort(z3_string_sort(ctx)))
non_digit <- z3_re_intersect(any_char, z3_re_complement(digit))
sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol, z3_in_re(s, z3_re_plus(digit)), z3_in_re(s, z3_re_star(non_digit)))
z3_check(sol)
#> [1] "unsat"

Note that z3_re_complement(digit) alone is every string except the one-character digit strings, including "12"; the intersection with any_char restricts it to single characters.

A password policy

A policy written as a regular expression: an uppercase letter, four to six lowercase letters, two or three digits, and ! or ?.

pw <- z3_string(ctx, "pw")
upper <- z3_re_range("A", "Z", ctx)
policy <- z3_re_concat(upper, z3_re_loop(lower, 4, 6), z3_re_loop(digit, 2, 3),
                       z3_re_union(z3_string_val(ctx, "!"), "?"))
sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol, z3_in_re(pw, policy), z3_length(pw) == 9,
       z3_prefixof("R", pw), z3_suffixof("!", pw))
z3_check(sol)
#> [1] "sat"
z3_value(z3_eval(z3_model(sol), pw))
#> [1] "Raaaaa00!"

The policy cannot produce a 14-character password:

sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol, z3_in_re(pw, policy), z3_length(pw) == 14)
z3_check(sol)
#> [1] "unsat"

Characters 

lambda <- z3_char_val(ctx, 955)
lambda
#> <z3_expr Unicode> (_ Char 955)
z3_value(z3_simplify(z3_char_to_int(lambda)))
#> [1] 955
z3_value(z3_simplify(z3_str_from_code(z3_int_val(ctx, 955))))
#> [1] "λ"
z3_value(z3_simplify(z3_char_is_digit(z3_char_val(ctx, 55))))
#> [1] TRUE

Sequences of any sort

The same operations work on sequences of integers, Booleans, or any other sort:

I <- z3_int_sort(ctx)
q <- z3_const(ctx, "q", z3_seq_sort(I))
u <- function(v) z3_seq_unit(z3_int_val(ctx, v))
sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol, z3_length(q) == 4, z3_seq_nth(q, 0) == 9,
       z3_contains(q, z3_concat(u(1), u(2))), z3_suffixof(u(5), q))
z3_check(sol)
#> [1] "sat"
z3_eval(z3_model(sol), q)
#> <z3_expr (Seq Int)> (seq.++ (seq.unit 9) (seq.unit 1) (seq.unit 2) (seq.unit 5))

Newer Z3 releases add higher-order sequence functions, whose function argument is a lambda:

x <- z3_int(ctx, "x")
z3_simplify(z3_seq_map(z3_lambda(x, x * 10), z3_concat(u(1), u(2), u(3))))
#> <z3_expr (Seq Int)> (seq.++ (seq.unit 10) (seq.unit 20) (seq.unit 30))
acc <- z3_int(ctx, "acc")
r <- z3_int(ctx, "r")
sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol, r == z3_seq_foldl(z3_lambda(list(acc, x), acc + x), 0, z3_concat(u(4), u(5), u(6))))
z3_check(sol)
#> [1] "sat"
z3_eval(z3_model(sol), r)
#> <z3_expr Int> 15
z3_value(z3_simplify(z3_replace_all(z3_string_val(ctx, "a-b-c"), "-", "+")))
#> [1] "a+b+c"

String solving is decidable only for fragments; with lengths, conversions to integers and regular expressions together, "unknown" answers are possible.
